title: assurance micro memo: quick SOC2 control probes
content:
Purpose / quick context:
- Short, informal scratch to capture immediate questions and simple mappings to speed up an evidence collection spike for SOC2 scoping. Not a final matrix.
- Focus: areas that tend to be messy for Redwood Private and Dedicated customers (network isolation, key management, customer-managed KMS, and audit logging for private control plane).

Notes to self / immediate asks:
- Ask SRE: where is the single source for ingress VPC peering docs for Private? I remember two, one in infra space and one in solutions eng. Need canonical link.
- Ask Platform Eng: can we produce a short statement / diagram that shows control plane separation for Private deployments (control plane in customer VPC vs Redwood-managed control plane)?
- Verify: Dedicated instances are on reserved GPU pools — does that mean we have a documented change management process for capacity changes (approve/notify customers)? Where is evidence of scheduled maintenance notices historically?

High-level risks I want captured (raw):
- Misaligned evidence: security team pulls logs from hosted control plane; customer private deployments use local logging — we might not have consolidated retention proof.
- KMS ambiguity: customers use their own KMS vs Redwood KMS - need to show how keys are handled, rotate, and who has access in emergency.
- Deployment drift: on-prem packages may be modified by customers; how do we document baseline and patch verification?

Control probe sketches (very rough):
- C-AUTH-01: SSO/IdP configuration and least-privilege roles
  - Evidence: SSO policy doc, sample SAML assertion mapping, last 90-day role review log, ticket assigning owner.
  - Owner: identity team (TBD)
  - Questions: Do we have automated monthly role recertification or manual? Slack thread about role sweeps?

- C-KMS-02: Key lifecycle for customer-managed KMS & Redwood-managed KMS
  - Evidence: KMS runbook, rotation schedule, HSM attestation (if used), sample audit log showing key access, KMS IAM policy snapshots.
  - Owner: infra-crypto (or sec-ops)
  - Unresolved: for Private deployments where customer brings KMS, what artifacts do we collect to show separation of duties? Customer attestation?

- C-LOG-03: Logging and retention coverage across Hosted / Dedicated / Private
  - Evidence: index of log sinks (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/ELK), retention config, example log export for a week, retention policy doc, retention expiration alerts.
  - Owner: observability
  - Practical: compile 2 weeks of example logs from each product mode, annotate where logs are not central.

- C-CHANGE-04: Change management for runtime or model rollouts that affect inference behavior
  - Evidence: rollout runbook, canary logs, post-deploy evaluation checklist, rollback ticket template.
  - Owner: release-engineering
  - Note: link to rollout automation PRs + console rollout config. Need copy of canary config used in last 3 release cycles.

- C-OPS-05: Incident response and detection coverage for inference runtime (latency/cost/regression incidents)
  - Evidence: incident report templates, 90/180-day incident list + postmortems, runbook for L7 incidents, contact matrix.
  - Owner: site-reliability-engineering
  - Gap: small incidents often handled via Slack threads; need exported timelines for audit.

Evidence naming convention (proposal):
- Use short structured names to avoid ad-hoc PDFs: e.g. soc2-C-KMS-02-kms-rotation-2025-10-21.log, soc2-C-LOG-03-elk-retention-2026-02-10.json, soc2-C-AUTH-01-role-review-2026-01.csv
- If we push this naming to owners it will make bulk packaging easier. TODO: ask legal if any artifact should be redacted before sharing with auditors.

Quick mapping for SOC2 criteria (tentative):
- Security (CC) — covers C-AUTH-01, C-KMS-02, C-LOG-03, C-CHANGE-04
- Availability — covers C-OPS-05, C-CHANGE-04
- Confidentiality — covers C-KMS-02, C-LOG-03 (access controls)

Questions to resolve (prioritize):
1) Private deployments: do we maintain any remote telemetry by default? If yes, where is the opt-out documented and does that affect evidence collection?
2) For customer-managed KMS, can customer provide a signed attestation PDF that we can stash in evidence? Is that acceptable to auditors?
3) Are backups for dedicated clusters encrypted at rest by default? Evidence: backup config snapshot + encryption keys used.
4) Where are historical maintenance notifications stored for Dedicated (to show communications re: planned downtime)?
5) For release rollouts that change model weights / quantization, can we produce a small eval script and results bundle that shows pre/post metrics for the change?

Quick TODO list (actionable):
- [ ] Ping Lena for latest KMS runbook and whether HSM attestation exists (deadline: 2026-03-02)
- [ ] Export one week of logs from Private demo cluster and annotate missing fields (deadline: 2026-03-07)
- [ ] Draft naming convention email and circulate to owners (deadline: 2026-03-01)
- [ ] Collect last three release-engineering canary configs + postmortem (deadline: 2026-03-10)
- [ ] Ask legal: acceptable customer attestation formats for KMS separation (deadline: 2026-03-04)

Random brainstorm (raw):
- Could we create a ‘SOC2-light snapshot’ tool that collects a predefined evidence bundle from a customer-controlled Private deployment (with their consent) and outputs a zip of named artifacts? This would accelerate evidence pulls for renewals.
- Consider small agent that runs on Private installs to verify baseline binaries/hashes and returns signed attestations to Redwood (opt-in only).

Notes-to-self (formatting + handoff):
- When packaging artifacts for auditors, include a 1-pager per control that lists: objective, tested evidence names (with timestamps), owner, and any compensating controls. Keep it short.
- Avoid sending raw Slack exports unless cleaned and annotated. Summarize threads with links to ticket IDs.

End — capture followups here so I can transfer to a formal Confluence control page after I have the first round of artifacts.
